newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma hugs 310, rates steady, bonds flat.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma hugs 310, rates steady, bonds flat.

text.p: The drachma was steady in early trading, with ecu/drachma hugging 310 and mark/drachma trading above 157. Depos were holding late Friday levels on unchanged interbank liquidity conditions, dealers said.
Bonds were sitting idle, looking to movements in money rates for clues.

"Depos and forex forwards are holding late Friday levels," said a money dealer at a private bank. "The market is quiet and I expect forex developments to have an impact on interbank liquidity and rates."

Anticipated monthly inflows from state pension funds should have a positive effect on liquidity and rates over the next few days but the central bank's depo tender on Wednesday would be a key factor in rate moves.
A facility of 14-day funds for 100 billion drachmas expires on Wednesday but so does a five-day repo pact of almost equal size.
"It is true that the net effect on liquidity would be negligible if the central bank chose not to hold the tender. That would be reassuring," the dealer said.
The Bank of Greece injected 96.8 billion drachmas in five-day securities repurchase funds at 12.90 percent on Friday. It fully satisfied all bids.
Bonds were fluctuating narrowly in subdued trading and dealers said they were closely watching liquidity developments in the interbank depo market.
"Bonds and flaoters are idling and the market is focusing on liquidity developments in the interbank market," a bond dealer said.
The dealer said trading activity in FRNs could pick up later when players from abroad come in.
The mark was quoted at 157.06/11 from Friday's 157.150 fix, the dollar at 281.47/57 drachmas from 281.600 and the ecu at 309.95/05 from 309.86 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is trading around 309.95/00 and mark/drachma around 157.10/15," a forex dealer said.

Ecu/drachma pierced the 310 level shortly after Friday's fixing when a large bank bought 100 million marks for drachmas. The market sold the marks at ecu/drachma rates equivalent to a level above 310 prompting some foreign banks to close out positions.
The central bank supplied the market with the amount of marks and ecus the market asked for in its Friday's afternoon window at ecu/drachma rates below 310.

"I think it would be better if the central bank supplied the amounts at the fixing, giving no bank the opportunity to profit by selling at 310.10/40 at the fixing and buying it from the central bank at 309.90 in the afternoon," a dealer said.
